title: The ambrosial Name
hookLine: sukhmanee sukh amrit prabh naam: this jewel of peace is the ambrosial Name (Sukhmani 24)

lines: A TITLE ON AN ORDINARY PAGE.
cards: Plenty of books take their title from one line buried inside them. You're reading along, and there on an ordinary page is the phrase from the cover, and suddenly the whole book makes a little more sense.
Sukhmani has a line like that. It isn't saved for the end. It's planted near the very beginning, and the bani's name comes from it.
As Sukhmani closes, we turn back to it: the ambrosial Name.

teach.h: RAHAO: THE PAUSE AT THE CENTER.
teach.b: The line comes right after Sukhmani's first stanza, marked rahao, which means pause: the place in a hymn where you stop and take in the center.
In paraphrase: Sukhmani, the jewel of peace, is the ambrosial Name of God; it rests in the minds of the devotees. Start with the name. Sukh is peace, ease, happiness.
Mani can be read as a jewel, so Sukhmani is often called the jewel of peace; some also hear man, the mind, in it: peace of mind. Either way, the line says what that jewel is. Not the poem.
The Name. Then amrit. In old Indian stories, amrit is the nectar of immortality, the drink of the gods.
In Gurbani it comes up again and again: the amrit vela before dawn, the amrit of the Name, the amrit Sikhs receive at initiation.
It means what gives true life, sweet and undying. And the last phrase: bhagat janaa kai man bisraam. Bisraam is rest, a place to stop and lay down a load, like a traveler's inn.
The Name is where the devotee's mind comes to rest. One way to read Sukhmani, then: all twenty-four ashtpadis, with their warnings and stories, their stillness and praise, unpack this one line.
Pride and humility, wealth and kindness, the wanderer and the beggar, the cleared eyes: each a way into the same rest.
Sukhmani's peace is not a mood. It's a Name, remembered.

how: Sikhs reciting Sukhmani Sahib pause at its rahao line, which calls the jewel of peace God's ambrosial Name, resting in the minds of devotees.

o: holy water kept for festival days
a sweet offered after the prayers
nectar, what gives true and undying life

games.q: the ambrosial Name — tap the pairs.
p: pause: the center of a hymn

s: Sukhmani's title line sits at the very end of the bani
it's the rahao near the beginning, and the bani's name comes from it.
Sukhmani is often called the jewel of peace
sukh is peace; mani can be read as jewel, and some hear man, the mind.
in the line, the jewel of peace is the poem itself
the line says the jewel of peace is God's ambrosial Name.

games.q: you've read all twenty-four ashtpadis. according to the rahao line, what is Sukhmani's jewel of peace?
games.why: the line says the jewel of peace is the amrit Name of God, resting in the minds of the devotees.

practice: Sit comfortably, let the body grow heavy, and with each breath set down one load, a worry, a task, a conversation, the way a traveler sets down a bag at an inn.
If you pray, let the Name, Waheguru, be the place where you set each one down; if you don't, let the breath itself be the resting place.

wordCard.voice: Amrit, the nectar of immortality: Sukhmani's rahao line says the jewel of peace is God's amrit Name, the place where the devotee's mind finds bisraam, rest.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: amrit, nectar of immortality; in Gurbani, what gives true, undying life.

carryVoice: Your line: the name is peace. A week walked; the bag can come off your shoulder. Five hundred thirty-two days now.
